However, if the policyholder outlives the coverage period, there is no payout.

Whole life insurance, on the other hand, provides coverage for the entirety of your life, as long as premiums are paid. This type of insurance offers a guaranteed death benefit and a cash value component that grows over time. The cash value can be accessed through policy loans or a policy surrender. Whole life insurance is generally more expensive than term life insurance but offers a more comprehensive coverage.

When choosing between term and whole life insurance, consider your financial commitments, the length of time you expect to need coverage, and your financial goals.
